1.

See [Xu, §1.8.1] for a discussion of the validity of the normality assumption needed to apply Braden’s theorem, and for an alternative proof using [DrG] instead on [Br] (and which therefore avoids this normality question).

2.

Explicity, the isomorphism in Proposition 5.6 is constructed as follows. Let

$t_{\mu}:T_{\mu}\to\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}\quad\text{and}\quad s_{\mu}:S_{\mu}\to\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$

be the embeddings, and consider also the natural maps

$\pi_{\mu}^{T}:T_{\mu}\to\{L_{\mu}\},\quad\pi_{\mu}^{S}:S_{\mu}\to\{L_{\mu}\},\quad i_{\mu}^{T}:\{L_{\mu}\}\to T_{\mu},\quad i_{\mu}^{S}:\{L_{\mu}\}\to S_{\mu}.$

By adjunction and the base change theorem, there exist canonical isomorphisms

$\Hom\bigl((i_{\mu}^{T})^{*}(t_{\mu})^{!}(-),(i_{\mu}^{S})^{!}(s_{\mu})^{*}(-)\bigr)\cong\Hom\bigl((t_{\mu})^{!}(-),(i_{\mu}^{T})_{*}(i_{\mu}^{S})^{!}(s_{\mu})^{*}(-)\bigr)\\
\cong\Hom\bigl((t_{\mu})^{!}(-),(t_{\mu})^{!}(s_{\mu})_{*}(s_{\mu})^{*}(-)\bigr);$

hence the adjunction morphism $\mathrm{id}\to(s_{\mu})_{*}(s_{\mu})^{*}$ induces a morphism of functors

$(i_{\mu}^{T})^{*}(t_{\mu})^{!}\to(i_{\mu}^{S})^{!}(s_{\mu})^{*}.$

Finally, one identifies the functors $(i_{\mu}^{T})^{*}$ and $(\pi^{T}_{\mu})_{*}$ , resp.  $(i_{\mu}^{S})^{!}$ and $(\pi^{S}_{\mu})_{!}$ , when applied to “weakly equivariant” objects; see [Br, Equation (1)].

In view of this proposition, for any $\mu\in X_{*}(T)$ we consider the functor

$\mathsf{F}_{\mu}:\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$

defined by

$\mathsf{F}_{\mu}(\mathscr{A})=\mathsf{H}^{\langle 2\rho,\mu\rangle}_{T_{\mu}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathscr{A})\cong\mathsf{H}^{\langle 2\rho,\mu\rangle}_{c}(S_{\mu},\mathscr{A}).$

Since the category $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ is semisimple (see Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.8), this functor is automatically exact.

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
